domainFirst.title: Let's put email on your domain
domainFirst.subtitle: Your domain. Your email. Your agents. All in one place. Four steps, and you can skip any of them.

domain.title: What is your domain?
domain.body: Email works on the domain you already have; no hosting needed.
domain.label: Your domain
domain.hint: Just the domain, no www or https.
domain.invalid: That does not look like a domain. Example: yourcompany.com
domain.skipped: Skipped for now. Come back here whenever you like.

dns.title: Publish the DNS records
dns.body: A few DNS records prove the domain is yours and let email leave it securely.
dns.unknown: We could not tell where DNS for {domain} lives. Pick it below or follow the general guide.
dns.manual: I'd rather add them by hand
dns.where: Where do you manage the domain's DNS?
dns.pending: We have not found every record yet. After you save them, DNS takes a few minutes to an hour to show up; we keep checking on our own.
dns.failed: Verification of {domain} timed out. Check the records and click Verify now again.
dns.verified: {domain} is verified: email can leave your domain now.
dns.skipped: Verification put off. The records stay in Domains.

registrobr.name: Registro.br
steps: Sign in at registro.br and open the domain.
Under DNS, click Configurar zona DNS and use Nova entrada for each record.
If the domain uses another company's DNS servers (your site's host, for example), the records go in that company's panel.

hostinger.name: Hostinger
steps: In hPanel, open Domains and pick the domain.
Under Manage DNS records, pick the type and copy the Name and Value of each row below.

godaddy.name: GoDaddy
steps: In My Products, find the domain and click DNS.
Pick the type and copy the Name and Value of each row below.

namecheap.name: Namecheap
steps: In Domain List, click Manage next to the domain.
Open the Advanced DNS tab and use Add New Record.
Copy the Host and Value of each row below. For the MX record, choose Custom MX under Mail Settings.

other.name: Other
steps: Open the panel where the domain's DNS is managed: usually where you bought the domain or your hosting.
Look for DNS Zone, DNS Records or Manage DNS.
Add each row below. If the Name field already shows the domain next to it, type only the part before it.

mailbox.title: Create your first mailbox
mailbox.body: Create an address on your domain, such as {address}, and read everything in Correio.
mailbox.locked: Once the domain is in DNS.
mailbox.done: You already have a mailbox in Correio.
mailbox.skipped: Mailbox put off. It is in Correio whenever you want it.

agent.title: Connect an agent (optional)
agent.body: Give an AI agent (Claude, Codex, Cursor and others) access to the mailbox over MCP, with a key you can revoke any time.

api.title: Rather start with the API?
api.body: Send a test email and get an API key. You can do it now, even without a domain.

title: Send your first email
subtitle: Test delivery and prepare your own API integration.

demo.title: Try a platform email
demo.body: This demonstration is sent from {from} only to {to}. No API key or domain setup is needed.

step1.title: Add an API key
step1.body: Keys authenticate every request. The full key is shown once, at creation.

step2.title: Send through the API
step2.bodyLocked: To your own inbox, from a domain you verify — the snippet unlocks once you have a key.
step2.bodyReady: Your key and your inbox are pre-filled. Verify your own domain, use a sender from it, then run the snippet from your terminal.
step2.subject: It works.
step2.sentTo: Send request accepted for {to}. Wait for the delivery event.
step2.selfHostBase: Self-hosted: set your SDK's base URL to {url}.
step2.sendLimited: A few onboarding emails already went out from this team. Try again in an hour.

step3.title: Watch it arrive
step3.waiting: waiting for your first email · checking every 5 s

success.title: Delivery confirmed
success.subtitle: Your team has confirmed deliveries. Review your current setup and send history below.
success.emailDelivered: Email sent · delivered to {to} in {seconds} s
success.counting: {count, plural, one {1 delivered. Counting.} other {# delivered. Counting.}}

attempt.label: Send history
attempt.inFlight: Send in transit — awaiting a delivery event. API acceptance is not delivery confirmation.
attempt.failed: This attempt ended without a confirmed delivery.
attempt.retryBody: Check the failure reason in the log and correct the recipient or sender settings before retrying. A new send happens only when you run the snippet or click the button.
attempt.readUnavailable: We could not load your current delivery status. Reload it before making another attempt; you can still open the email history.

next.label: Next step
next.addTitle: Add your domain to send to anyone
next.addBody: For now MepMail only sends the test to your own address. With your domain verified, you send from hello@yourcompany.com to any address. It takes three DNS records, and the page checks on its own until they show up.
next.finishBody: The DNS records are still missing. Publish them at your provider before {deadline}: the domain page shows what to copy and checks again every 30 seconds.

explore.label: Explore more

mcp.title: Install MCP
mcp.body: Connect your AI tools and agents to send email through MepMail.

webhooks.title: Set up webhooks
webhooks.body: Delivery events, pushed to your endpoint as they happen.

team.title: Invite your team
team.body: Members manage emails, domains, and webhooks.

migrate.title: Migrate from Resend
migrate.body: One command moves contacts, segments, templates, webhooks and domains.

explore.instance: Send rate and email retention are instance settings — set them in <link>Settings</link>.

stepSes.title: Connect your AWS SES
stepSes.body: MepMail sends through your own AWS SES account. Connect it once in settings — the wizard creates everything and tests the connection.
